newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo precious metals weaker in bearish sentiment.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo precious metals weaker in bearish sentiment.

text.p: Yen-based Tokyo precious metals futures settled mostly weaker on Friday, pressured by weak spot prices and the yen's firmer tendency against the dollar, traders said.
Gold futures ranged from three to seven yen per gram lower. Benchmark October was down five yen per gram at 1,363 yen.
"Bearish sentiment in spot gold dragged down Tokyo gold futures. Most private investors were sidelined on seeing that the yen's slip had stalled," one trader said.
Bullion was quoted at $377.80/378.10 per ounce at the Tokyo close, against $377.90/378.40 in New York on Thursday.
Activity in gold futures was mostly dominated by inter-month trade by trade houses which were trading in line with the currency market.

Spot gold edged lower due mainly to Australian producer selling before paring some of early losses on short-covering. Traders expected more producer selling to emerge in the near term. "Spot gold could probe strong support at $377.50 per ounce," one trader said.
Platinum futures dipped in tandem with weaker spot platinum prices. Prices ranged from three to six yen per gram lower, with benchmark October ending three down at 1,377 yen.

Market sentiment in platinum was dampened after spot platinum fell below support at $380.00 per ounce during Asian hours. Spot platinum was quoted at $379.25/380.00 per ounce at the Tokyo close after opening at $380.00/75.
Silver futures ranged from 0.7 yen to 2.1 yen per 10 grams lower. Benchmark October was down 0.7 yen at 178.4 yen.
Palladium futures were mixed. Prices ranged from five yen per gram lower to three yen up. Benchmark October was one yen up at 427 yen. -- Tokyo Commodity Desk +81-3-3432-7431 --
